fields.title: 📖 Miʿrāǧ, Ruʾyah, and blanket Takfīr – the documented Ikhtilāf
fields.body:
<!-- slide: 1 -->
# Miʿrāǧ with the body: the majority position

🖋️ Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ رحمه الله

“The majority of the Salaf and of the Muslims held that it took place with the body and in a waking state.”

He explains this view to be correct.

The affirmation of the real Isrāʾ and Miʿrāǧ with body and soul is thereby documented as the majority view of the Salaf and the Muslims.

📝 Source: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, aš-Šifāʾ, Faṣl Ḥaqīqat al-Isrāʾ

[→ Source library Q36](/q/36/)

<!-- slide: 2 -->
# The early scholars on the manner of the Isrāʾ

🖋️ Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ رحمه الله

“The Salaf and the scholars disagreed: did his Isrāʾ take place with his soul or with his body?”

He documents three transmitted views.

The majority position and this actual early Ikhtilāf are to be kept apart.

📝 Source: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, aš-Šifāʾ, Ḥaqīqat al-Isrāʾ

[→ Source library Q36](/q/36/)

<!-- slide: 3 -->
# The authentic wording of ʿĀʾišah

🖋️ ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها

“Whoever claims that Muḥammad ﷺ saw his Lord has uttered a tremendous false claim against Allah.”

The transmitted expression is: “faqad aʿẓama ʿalā Allāhi al-firyah”.

This report does not expressly state: “Whoever believes that is a Kāfir.” The wording must not be rewritten into another statement.

📝 Source: Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 177, report of ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها

[→ Source library Q36](/q/36/)

<!-- slide: 4 -->
# Ibn ʿAbbās: He saw Him with the heart

🖋️ ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما

Concerning the verses “The heart did not lie about what it saw” and “Indeed, he saw Him another time,” he said:

“He saw Him with his heart twice.”

This is the heart-Ruʾyah authentically transmitted in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim. It is not to be equated with an express claim about the bodily eyes.

📝 Source: Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 176, from Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما

[→ Source library Q36](/q/36/)

<!-- slide: 5 -->
# Ibn Ḥaǧar: the documented Ruʾyah-Ikhtilāf

🖋️ Ibn Ḥaǧar رحمه الله

He documents various transmitted positions: ʿĀʾišah and Ibn Masʿūd denied the Ruʾyah; from Abū Ḏarr there were differing reports; another group affirmed it.

He also mentions the affirming statement of al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī and the transmission of ʿUrwah ibn az-Zubayr.

The classical sources treat this as a transmitted Ikhtilāf and not as a simple formula “Muslim or Kāfir”.

📝 Source: Ibn Ḥaǧar, Fatḥ al-Bārī, section on the Ikhtilāf of the Salaf concerning the Ruʾyah

[→ Source library Q36](/q/36/)

<!-- slide: 6 -->
# Ibn Taymiyyah: heart-Ruʾyah and eye-Ruʾyah

🖋️ Ibn Taymiyyah رحمه الله

He affirms that it is transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās in authentic reports:

“Muḥammad saw his Lord with his heart twice.”

At the same time he explains that no authentic express wording from Ibn ʿAbbās is established according to which he saw Him with his bodily eyes.

Therefore heart-Ruʾyah and eye-Ruʾyah must not be confused with one another.

📝 Source: Ibn Taymiyyah, Maǧmūʿ al-Fatāwā 6/509

[→ Source library Q36](/q/36/)

<!-- slide: 7 -->
# Two separate questions: Miʿrāǧ and Ruʾyah

The affirmation of the bodily Isrāʾ and Miʿrāǧ concerns the real ascent of the Prophet ﷺ.

The question of how the Ruʾyah is transmitted and understood is to be kept apart from that. The authentically reported heart-Ruʾyah is not automatically an eye-Ruʾyah either.

The bodily ascent must moreover not be understood as a claim of spatial co-location with Allah.

This distinction follows from the evidences named before.

📝 Source: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, aš-Šifāʾ; Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 176–177; Ibn Taymiyyah, Maǧmūʿ al-Fatāwā 6/509

[→ Source library Q36](/q/36/)

<!-- slide: 8 -->
# Conclusion: no invented blanket Takfīr

The bodily Isrāʾ and Miʿrāǧ is documented as the majority view of the Salaf and the Muslims. Concerning the Ruʾyah, an actual Ikhtilāf was transmitted from the early scholars.

ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها denied the Ruʾyah sharply. Her authentic report does not, however, contain the express formula “Whoever believes this is a Kāfir.”

From Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما the heart-Ruʾyah is authentically transmitted.

The positions must not be mixed together or reformulated into a blanket Takfīr.

📝 Source: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, aš-Šifāʾ; Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 176–177; Ibn Ḥaǧar, Fatḥ al-Bārī; Ibn Taymiyyah, Maǧmūʿ al-Fatāwā 6/509

[→ Source library Q36](/q/36/)
